# Interaction learning: How are credit and teacher information assigned after standardizing trajectories?

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/agent-research/agent-policy-learning.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-24 · 58 topic entries / 11 representative comparisons

Agent Lightning turns execution into trainable transitions. GiGPO, AdaStep, and DepGPO assign credit using repeated states, return variance, and command dependencies, respectively. Frontier-OPD and ASTEROID change how teacher data reaches students. Recording a trajectory is only the entry point; objectives and information access define the algorithms.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

Axes: Whether supervision units are tokens, environment steps, command dependencies, or expert trajectories · Whether local credit depends on recurrent states, stochastic returns, or trusted tracing · Whether teachers supply distributions or short bridges versus complete successful episodes · Whether privileged information stays on the training side or enters deployment input

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Local credit is trustworthy only when its evidence is trustworthy

GiGPO complements global advantage with return comparisons within a shared anchor. AdaStep asks how much variation is explained by actions versus random continuation. DepGPO instead uses actual file, stdout, and verifier dependencies, without requiring recurrent states. These are not interchangeable step rewards. Fine-grained numbers do not add evidence without trustworthy states or traces. Agent Lightning's common transitions help connect algorithms but do not supply missing conditions.

Sources: [GiGPO](../../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en.md) · [AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../agent-research/2610.03223-adastep/README-en.md) · [Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.03634-depgpo/README-en.md) · [Agent Lightning](../../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en.md)

### Teachers change training data, not what deployment can see

Frontier-OPD selects short intervention from student-visited states. Compare a window matching actual bridge length plus continuation, and add only teacher bridge responses. ASTEROID conditions on exploration history and then supplies a full success for the same hidden task, covering contexts outside smooth expert openings. Teacher units and objectives differ. Deployment sees only public observations and its own history, not hidden tasks, gold, or future outcomes inserted for convenient replay.

Sources: [Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond](../../../../agent-research/2610.32802-frontier-opd/README-en.md) · [Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration](../../../../agent-research/2610.30105-asteroid/README-en.md)

### When trajectories become training data, objective boundaries matter more than shared interfaces

Agent Lightning turns heterogeneous execution into attributable transitions. Instruct-to-Act binds language to non-overlapping intervals within one episode and marks instruction completion at the end. Unannotated valid steps have no BC but remain stop negatives; padding affects neither. RSSM, actor/value training and real rollouts remain necessary.

Sources: [Decoupling Planning and Control for Instructable Agents](../../../../agent-research/2608.26788-instruct-to-act/README-en.md) · [Agent Lightning](../../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en.md)

### Group-relative credit begins with what each group compares

GiGPO separates whole-trajectory reward from action differences at a shared anchor state. ACE-RL groups actor tasks, reflector seeds and curator reflections, valuing edits through new execution rather than prose scoring. Shared centering does not equal shared provenance, counterfactuals or information boundaries. Singleton filters/token reductions also change training and cannot be hidden in one generic normalizer.

Sources: [Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement](../../../../agent-research/2611.16409-ace-rl/README-en.md) · [GiGPO](../../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en.md)

### From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents

At warmup checkpoints8/16/24/32, candidate LoRA gradients combine with frozen first/second Adam moments into a ranking feature. Bias correction is omitted, so this is not a full AdamW update. Each public-support gradient is unit-normalized before its family mean; normalized candidate features are dotted with these means, averaged across checkpoints, then maximized across families. Forty public support actions contain no evaluation-query answers. Global selection exactly deduplicates complete message contents, keeps first representative indices, selects256 contents and replays three shuffled passes for768 presentations. Matched selection preserves every reference task/action position and distinct-content quota. Final students restart from the original base, not warmup weights. Controls check checkpoint/family order, no renormalization of the support mean, unchanged random sampling under duplicate rows, first-index score ties, complete shuffled passes, matched access to nonreference contents in the same stratum, rejection of cross-stratum duplicate contents, and rejection of NaNs, negative second moments and intermediate overflow. Seeds change synthetic inputs and schedules, not independently trained models.

Sources: [From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.27159-acting-to-learning/README-en.md) · [What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2608.27260-ace-data/README-en.md)

### $R^2$: Recognizing and Reducing Redundant Visual Tool Use

VFD replaces only the current feedback while retaining the source image, other history and scored reasoning tokens. It subtracts mean log probability under three same-sized nonoverlapping random crops from that under actual feedback. During the first10%of training, source-specific30th-percentile thresholds use reasoning windows only, then freeze. Direct-answer windows may be scored later but cannot initialize thresholds. One uniformly sampled eligible call estimates the redundant count byMtimes its indicator; unavailable scores with complete records set the indicator to1, and empty eligible sets cost0. Tool-Independent adds0.5times all calls. Efficiency advantages are centered only among correct trajectories, divided by fixed call budget4, and added with weight0.2 to outcome advantages. Cheap failures receive no efficiency reward. Controls cover zero VFD for identical feedback scores, exclusion of answer windows from calibration, rejection of missing-source warmup, strict threshold inequality, unavailable-score versus empty-eligible behavior, one-call sampling rather than full counting, zero efficiency terms for failures, zero-sum correct-set efficiency, all-wrong/single-correct/equal-cost cases, negative-advantage clipping, padding exclusion and intermediate-overflow rejection. Three seeds of numerical controls do not establish tool-efficiency or accuracy gains.

Sources: [$R^2$: Recognizing and Reducing Redundant Visual Tool Use](../../../../agent-research/2611.27070-r2-tool-redundancy/README-en.md) · [AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../agent-research/2610.03223-adastep/README-en.md)

### Optimistic Online Learning for Coding Agents with Aggregate Feedback

The distribution is not softmax: FTRL combines Tsallis and log-barrier terms. It uses completed-task scores, previous hints in the current task and the current hint weighted by elapsed turns. A task draws one Exp(1) noise vector shared across all turns and selects argmin noise/probability. The probability rho that arm k wins every turn uses maxima of probability ratios, not products of marginals. Only that event receives residual Z/rho; switched tasks have zero residual correction while every arm still receives accumulated hints. Algorithm2 doubles its threshold when a signed cumulative observable potential gap strictly exceeds it, resetting score and gap rather than clipping negative gaps. Controls check KKT residuals, translation invariance, shared-noise event probabilities versus independent products, zero residual attribution after switching, elapsed-turn hint weighting, task bounds, lifecycle errors, preserved pending state after invalid aggregates, signed negative gaps and restart resets. Analytic event partitions check importance weighting; a small Monte Carlo run is not advertised as proof of unbiasedness.

Sources: [Optimistic Online Learning for Coding Agents with Aggregate Feedback](../../../../agent-research/2611.30405-ooas/README-en.md) · [From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.27159-acting-to-learning/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### When outcomes vary widely after the same action, why do GiGPO, AdaStep, and DepGPO need different evidence? {#cross-local-credit-evidence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** GiGPO compares local returns across actions at one anchor. AdaStep uses within-action and total variance to assess reliability and reduces correction under high continuation randomness. DepGPO checks whether command outputs reach the verifier by dependencies rather than using within-action variance. Choose evidence according to reliable recurrent states or tracing; synthetic anchors cannot establish a fair real-state comparison.

    **Illustrative example:** Incorrect answers after identical searches may reflect later writing variation. A terminal task can instead check whether a write command supplied data consumed by the final test.

    Sources: [GiGPO](../../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en.md) · [AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../agent-research/2610.03223-adastep/README-en.md) · [Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.03634-depgpo/README-en.md)

### Why can't Frontier-OPD teacher bridges and ASTEROID expert successes both be reduced to one expert label at the current state? {#cross-bridge-versus-successful-episode}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Frontier-OPD uses a short bridge to change reachable continuation and admits responses by equal-length agreement over bridge plus student continuation. ASTEROID conditions on student exploration before learning from a complete same-task expert episode; BAMDP preserves hidden tasks across episodes. A single label erases differences in context, collection units, and admission.

    **Illustrative example:** Briefly helping a student past a blockage and returning control is not the same training example as a whole expert success after two student trials.

    Sources: [Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond](../../../../agent-research/2610.32802-frontier-opd/README-en.md) · [Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration](../../../../agent-research/2610.30105-asteroid/README-en.md)

### When does connecting Agent Lightning transitions to GiGPO or Frontier-OPD count as training integration? {#cross-transition-log-versus-actual-update}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Records must contain required state, sampling policy, and permitted supervision. The trainer must update parameters with the appropriate advantage or distillation objective and evaluate. GiGPO needs valid anchor groups; Frontier-OPD needs original histories, valid bridges, and training-pool isolation. Names, counts, and callbacks are insufficient. Local controlled patch updates and L1 contracts are not LLM policy training.

    **Illustrative example:** A thousand actions without shared-state identity or frozen teacher/student probabilities cannot compute micro advantages or validate teacher bridge admission.

    Sources: [Agent Lightning](../../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en.md) · [GiGPO](../../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en.md) · [Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond](../../../../agent-research/2610.32802-frontier-opd/README-en.md)

### Do correct BC and stop losses reproduce the language world-model controller? {#cross-cross-colm-instruct-to-act}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. RSSM model/actor/value learning, real rollouts, instruction embeddings and annotation are still required. Local code executes two auxiliary objectives without replacing missing networks.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: correct gradients do not establish diamond collection in Minecraft.

    Sources: [Decoupling Planning and Control for Instructable Agents](../../../../agent-research/2608.26788-instruct-to-act/README-en.md) · [Agent Lightning](../../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en.md)

### Does one task-level GRPO group combining actors, reflectors and curators preserve ACE-RL? {#cross-cross-nov15-ace-rl}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Their rewards and comparison provenance differ. Preserve seed/reflection groups before concatenating generated tokens for a shared update.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: three edits from one reflection compare with each other, not directly with a separate actor's task score.

    Sources: [Experience-Handoff Reinforcement Learning for Recursive Self-Improvement](../../../../agent-research/2611.16409-ace-rl/README-en.md) · [GiGPO](../../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en.md)

### What does this study control beyond ACE Lens? {#cross-cross-nov23-acting-to-learning}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** It separates the ranking rule from its admissible selection space. Global random and high-NLL share the gradient selector's freedom to change coverage, avoiding a confound from unequal freedom.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: if gradient selects256records globally, random must also have global freedom rather than being forced to preserve old task quotas.

    Sources: [From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.27159-acting-to-learning/README-en.md) · [What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2608.27260-ace-data/README-en.md)

### Can R² and AdaStep exchange their statistics? {#cross-cross-nov23-r2-tool-redundancy}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. AdaStep uses action-group return variance at a shared state to estimate credit reliability. R² uses same-text feedback likelihood differences for costs, then compares correct outputs only. Their conditioning and normalization differ.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a repeated crop may have near-zeroVFD despite stable later returns; stability does not make the observation nonredundant.

    Sources: [$R^2$: Recognizing and Reducing Redundant Visual Tool Use](../../../../agent-research/2611.27070-r2-tool-redundancy/README-en.md) · [AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../agent-research/2610.03223-adastep/README-en.md)

### Do the two selectors choose the same object at the same time? {#cross-cross-nov24-ooas}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. The earlier paper selects historical actions for SFT; OOAS chooses steering policies online and updates after aggregate feedback. Offline gradient scores do not automatically satisfy its hint/regret assumptions.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: choosing256 cleaning records selects training data; choosing Cap1.5 versus2.0 selects a current intervention.

    Sources: [Optimistic Online Learning for Coding Agents with Aggregate Feedback](../../../../agent-research/2611.30405-ooas/README-en.md) · [From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.27159-acting-to-learning/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

**2026-11-24** · The independent standard-library CPU kernel solves FTRL's KKT equations: Gk+alpha/sqrt(pk)+beta/pk share a multiplier, found by score translation and bisection rather than a softmax substitute. It implements shared exponential sampling, rho, aggregate residuals, the potential and Algorithm2 restarts. The begin/choose/finish API receives current hints and one terminal aggregate, not turn reward vectors or gold answers/plans. Injected noise is for mathematical controls only. No LLM, activation probe, TACT intervention, code executor, real-task score or Evolve mapping runs. The float64 root solver has numerical tolerance, not infinite precision. The full campaign is terminally not reproduced.

Affected: [Optimistic Online Learning for Coding Agents with Aggregate Feedback](../../../../agent-research/2611.30405-ooas/README-en.md) · [From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.27159-acting-to-learning/README-en.md)

**2026-11-23** · The CPU NumPy slice computes same-text token-log-probability VFD, reasoning-only source-frozen thresholds, one-eligible-call redundancy estimation and category base costs, sample-SD outcome advantages, correct-only efficiency terms and a clipped GRPO scalar. Linear quantile interpolation and mean-valid-tokens-per-trajectory then group averaging are explicit local conventions, not bitwise equivalence to an unreleased trainer. Callers must supply aligned reasoning windows, valid crops and complete records; arrays cannot establish those semantics. No VLM, crop construction/scoring, CAT rollout labeling, images, policy backprop/update or visual-agent evaluation runs. Finite differences check a scalar derivative, not training. There is no gold-answer/plan interface;binary rewards are external trainer/evaluator inputs. Full experiments are terminally not reproduced.

Affected: [$R^2$: Recognizing and Reducing Redundant Visual Tool Use](../../../../agent-research/2611.27070-r2-tool-redundancy/README-en.md) · [AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../agent-research/2610.03223-adastep/README-en.md)

**2026-11-23** · The independent NumPy float64 slice implements explicit-gradient/frozen-moment features, individually normalized support gradients, checkpoint averaging before family maximization, exact full-string deduplication, global top/random selection with three replay passes, and reference-position/stratum distinct-content quotas. Undefined zero-norm directions and intermediate feature overflow are rejected, not assigned invented scores. Synthetic gradients and historical-action strings exercise the formulas; lexical similarity does not replace gradients. No LoRA extraction, warmup training, ALFWorld, Qwen checkpoint, deployment executor, student SFT or capability comparison runs. Callers must ensure support is public training-side information rather than query answers. Full experiments are terminally not reproduced.
